question: Can the pinned small native decision model run complete short requests correctly and cheaply enough on CPU to justify later workload qualification?
scope: Compatibility, bounded latency and existing ticket-routing diagnostic; not fresh held-out community evidence, model selection or production throughput proof.

gate.warmup: First routing case, normal order; excluded from diagnostic metrics
gate.criterion: Every call must return a valid native response; label correctness is recorded but does not control continuation. Gate calls are excluded from the 48-row cohort.
gate.interpretation: An experiment spending limit, not a production latency SLO.

routing_schedule: All 24 existing cases in fixture order, each normal then reverse candidate order, exactly once: 48 correlated observations.
preflight: Before semantic inference, check every planned request with the pinned native Julia template and actual tokenizer. Reject per-option/head truncation and whole-prompt overflow; do not shorten questions, options or evidence.
stop: Stop at first transport error, timeout, invalid response, preflight failure or budget exhaustion. Preserve all planned rows with not_run/interrupted status and null cohort accuracy/median/p95 if incomplete.
resources: Record cgroup memory.peak, limits, effective runtime arguments, image/binary/model/source hashes and concurrent Docker workloads. Verify owned runtime stops; leave unrelated containers untouched.
comparison_limit: Different model precision (Julia Q8 vs earlier Kev/Qwen Q4), context, batching, memory cap and host contention prevent an intrinsic speedup claim from earlier runs. No CPU result establishes Metal, AMD64, CUDA, long-context quality or calibrated confidence.
